name: tilt-shift
title: Tilt-shift miniature
summary: A real-looking town seen from high above through a tilted lens and a time-lapse clock, so the whole world reads as a tabletop model.

look.ground: a town or landscape seen from 100-200 m, oblique 45-55 degrees or straight down

palette.where: streets and squares, dark so markings pop
trees and parks, very saturated in daylight
candy roofs, vehicles, the one subject to find
dawn and night states, the only low-saturation ones

look.type: the place's own signage: an open highway-sign font (Overpass) on sign-coloured panels inside the lower blur band; a monospace time-lapse clock with a speed readout
look.texture: a horizontal sharp band, everything above and below melting into depth-of-field blur; vignette
look.light: a hard sun with sharp blue shadows, the azimuth cheated per shot to front-light the facades; low warm ground bounce
look.materials: photoreal but model-like: varied window bays, grime, glossy vehicles, people as small colour capsules

consistency: one place built once and revisited at different hours; hero actors 20-30 % larger than real so they read

motion.feel: time-lapse stutter: the world steps at ~8 Hz on the beat while the camera stays smooth
moves: world updates held for several frames (8 Hz = 3 frames at 24 fps), camera smooth on every frame
the sharp band slides to follow one subject
dive from high to actor height with a speed ramp, stutter vanishing below about x2
vertical rise with logarithmic height for a summary

pace.text: signage subtitles held at least max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s); a clock readout whenever speed changes

banned: street-level shots except one deliberate close-up
dissolves that reveal the fake lens
a fixed sun that leaves half the film backlit
source: LemoLab's Tilt-Shift Miniature style in lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar at 9eb7739; pace measured with analyze.py and events.py on its demo film "Toy Town Rush Hour"
